answer: Asymmetric Storage Proof Depletion Agents store rotating micro-shards of uncompressible data on regional shale nodes to prove continuous resource commitment. Each active identity must independently refresh these memory allocations at fixed intervals, preventing cheap parallel replication. The attacker pays a linear hardware-rental cost multiplied by the identity count, scaling until mass duplication drains their capital faster than the local economic garden yields returns. To fund this, every agent locks a tiny jade reserve that permanently decays if retrieval proofs fail.
